items.title: Scalar finite-element substructuring model
items.statement: Fix the 2D scalar diffusion finite-element model, its matching shape-regular P1 subdomain meshes, local energy forms, interface and interior degrees of freedom, and the global Dirichlet problem.

items.title: Eigenvalue bounds from a left-inverse preconditioner
items.statement: If A is SPD and LT=I, the eigenvalues of (LA^{-1}L^T)(T^TAT) lie between 1 and the squared A-operator norm of TL.

items.title: Floating local kernels and positive interior blocks
items.statement: On a connected triangulated subdomain the Neumann diffusion energy has exactly the constant functions as its kernel, while the interior stiffness block with zero boundary trace is positive definite.

items.title: Primal interface spaces and jump convention
items.statement: Define broken, fully assembled and partially assembled interface spaces, primal corner and edge-average constraints, the jump map, and the redundant-multiplier range convention.

items.title: Primal constraints remove local floating kernels
items.statement: If each connected floating subdomain component has an anchored primal vertex and the global Dirichlet boundary is nonempty, the partially assembled energy is positive definite and each local dual solve is uniquely solvable.

items.title: Discrete harmonic extension and interface Schur complement
items.statement: Define the local discrete harmonic extension, the local interface Schur complement, and the assembled and partially assembled interface operators by eliminating interior degrees of freedom.

items.title: Discrete harmonic extension minimizes energy
items.statement: For fixed admissible interface values, the discrete harmonic extension is the unique local finite-element energy minimizer, and its energy equals the Schur-complement quadratic form.

items.title: Static condensation is the exact interface problem
items.statement: Block elimination of all subdomain interior variables gives an exactly equivalent interface Schur system, and harmonic reconstruction recovers the unique global finite-element solution.

items.title: Coefficient-scaled averaging and BDDC
items.statement: Define a partition-of-unity scaled averaging projection, the BDDC interface preconditioner, and its constrained partially assembled minimization problem.

items.title: BDDC is the constrained partial-energy minimizer
items.statement: For each assembled residual, the partially assembled BDDC solve is the unique minimizer of the strictly convex partial energy minus the averaged residual work, and averaging returns its conforming correction.

items.title: FETI-DP dual system and preconditioner
items.statement: Define the FETI-DP saddle system, multiplier Schur operator on the range of the jump map, coefficient-scaled right inverse, and dual preconditioner.

items.title: Discrete Schur energy and the fractional trace norm
items.statement: For shape-regular polygonal subdomains and matching quasiuniform P1 meshes, the local Schur energy modulo constants is uniformly equivalent to the intrinsic H1/2 boundary seminorm, with a boundary-preserving finite-element lifting.

items.title: FETI-DP is the exact dual Schur system
items.statement: Eliminating the partially assembled displacement from the FETI-DP saddle equations gives the positive-definite multiplier Schur system, and the exact multiplier solution reconstructs the conforming interface solution.

items.title: Complementary primal and dual projections share nonunit spectrum
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional SPD energy and complementary primal and dual projections satisfying the BDDC/FETI-DP right-inverse identities, the two preconditioned operators have the same eigenvalues, with multiplicities, away from the eigenvalue one.

items.title: Two-dimensional logarithmic edge cutoff estimates
items.statement: The piecewise-linear edge cutoff has squared H1/2_00 norm O(1+log(H/h)); multiplication by it costs at most the squared logarithm after the discrete P1 L-infinity bound, which is proved from a cone estimate.

items.title: Conditioning and solver work are separate claims
items.statement: The condition-number estimate controls ideal preconditioned iteration counts, not total work; local and coarse factorization costs depend on solver choices and coarse dimension.

items.title: BDDC and FETI-DP have matching nontrivial spectra
items.statement: With identical primal constraints and coefficient scalings, the quotient-space BDDC and FETI-DP operators have the same positive eigenvalues except possibly for one; any zero modes from redundant multiplier coordinates disappear under the declared range convention.

items.title: Two-dimensional scaled averaging energy bound
items.statement: For scalar diffusion with positive subdomain-constant coefficients, all subdomain vertices primal, bounded polygon shape complexity, and matching quasiuniform shape-regular 2D P1 meshes, the scaled jump projection has energy norm at most C(1+log(H/h)).

items.title: The two-dimensional BDDC and FETI-DP polylogarithmic bound
items.statement: For the stated scalar second-order 2D diffusion family, both BDDC and FETI-DP preconditioned condition numbers are bounded by C(1+log(H/h))^2, independent of h, H, subdomain count, and positive subdomain-constant coefficient jumps.

items.title: A floating component with no primal corner remains singular
items.statement: A floating local Laplace stiffness block with no primal anchor retains its constant null vector, so the local dual solve is not uniquely defined.

items.title: Two floating Poisson subdomains and primal anchoring
items.statement: Compute the local floating Poisson stiffness kernel on two matching square subdomains, show how primal corner values remove the local constant modes, and identify the resulting exact interface solve.

items.title: A finite-dimensional BDDC/FETI-DP spectral match
items.statement: For a two-coordinate SPD interface energy with one primal and one dual coordinate, compute the BDDC and FETI-DP preconditioned eigenvalue and verify that both equal 4/3.

items.title: A dense coarse solve can dominate local work
items.statement: In a dense direct-solve cost model, increasing the number of primal constraints can make the cubic coarse factorization dominate parallel local factorizations even when the condition number bound is unchanged.
